ops.title: No sound wedged-vs-busy test exists for codex-ask workers; reaper rejected
ops.body:
Decision 2026-09-03: task eed02b8 (bound a wedged detached codex-ask worker) closed as won't-do after investigation.

Three candidate signals, all refuted:
- Elapsed age: codex runs carry no timeout anywhere — none in the argv dispatch.go builds, none in watchMode. Runs are unbounded by design, so age carries no information at all.
- Log silence (best candidate): the lane log is per-tool-call JSONL, but item.started carries "aggregated_output":"" and nothing further is written for that item until it completes. One long shell command yields a legitimate silent gap spanning its whole duration; a go test -race run took 931s on this host. Any threshold short enough to be useful has a live false-positive path.
- CPU-time delta: a worker waiting on the model API burns zero CPU. Idle != wedged.

The asymmetry is what settles it. detach.go runWorker writes status in a deferred atomicWrite and renames ReplyTmp->Reply; on SIGKILL neither runs, so the lane classifies 'died' and both the result and the API spend are lost. A wedged worker, by contrast, costs one idle process — and since the P4 sweep landed, its run dir is collected once aged.

The reporting half already exists: psRecord.LogAgeS (log_age_s) is emitted for every lane, so a human or agent can already observe silence and decide.

If ever revisited, one sub-case IS sound: worker alive, no status file, and no live codex descendant. runWorker writes status in a defer immediately after runCodex returns, and the only post-codex work (wakeOwner, registerTranscript) is bounded at 30s — so a worker in that state for minutes is provably stuck. It catches only the 'codex already exited' wedge, not the likelier one, and costs a process-tree walk per lane.
